productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I feel like I'm cheating on Joshua Dunbar, Teresa Goodridge, and Ava Browne (and an honorable mention for Jennifer Stay from Coloring Bliss for her early gnomes), with this purchase. As far as I'm concerned, they have the best gnome images.  Dunbar's Gnomes not only made me realize I could enjoy coloring figures, but also made me realize that I really enjoy coloring fantasy houses.  He managed to capture a level of magic, and humor I hadn't seen a lot of, in "adult coloring books."  Goodridge made me crack, and give into the "nose gnome" phenomenon, because her images went above and beyond with tons of charming, little humorous details, retaining a lot of her own distinctive style.  And, Browne's Medieval Gnomes was just deliciously unique, with a high fantasy vein, so different from everyone else's take on gnomes.  Coco Wyo has managed to come up with some scenes that are too playfully cute to pass up on, even for this sarcastic cynic.  It's hard to pick favorite images here, because they're all so darn cute.  The absolute favorite is probably the one with the cauldron.  The one that made me laugh out loud was the hedgehog, wearing a headlamp, leading the gnome into the forest.  I can see myself coloring most of the images.  The fact that these are all about medium, in difficulty level, was the big selling point.  While looking through my "short list" of interesting, fairly recently released books, I decided to pick a few that don't have super detailed images.  Coloring cute, less busy pages seems to be what I enjoy most.  I've reached a point with my adult coloring book collection that I'm going to have to stop buying books for a long time, because I don't have space for more books.  I can't change the amount of physical space available to me, so I'm going to have to buckle down, not buy anything, and just have to color what I have.  While I do plan on getting rid of some books, they aren't going to clear out much storage space.  With my limited income--and lack of space--I never should have spent so much, on so many books.Printing wise... This is an Amazon print-on-demand, KDP title.  It's printed single-sided, with black toner on the reverse, but no duplicate images (I actually like duplicates, but that's ok). The first page is an adorable lead in page, with some text.  Compared to some other Coco Wyo books, the sign's text is well-written in English--and doesn't sound like awkward English as a second language.  Then, there are a few pages of front matter (tips, social media information), followed by a cute, but simple nameplate page, and one color test page.  At the back, my copy has one entirely blank page (front and back), and one that has the printing location and date, on the back.  I don't mind the blank pages.Overall, I really like this book.  It's a little too heavy on Christmas-themed pages, for my taste.  However, I'm not religious.  And, I don't have much family left. So, I find holidays mean very little to me.  I would have rather had another image or two geared toward Halloween, generic spooky, or generic autumn.  This book was still a good value, however.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: These are such cute coloring books!  I think they are great for kids, teens, and adults who like to color. productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I'm really not a winter holiday person.  If I could hibernate from November 1st to June 1st, I would gladly.  Once again, this book is so cute, it's disgustingly irresistible.  Even with all the pretty heavily patterned fabrics, and copious other details oozing good cheer, I can't help but like the images (I really don't enjoy coloring the "entangled" or "Zentangle-inspired" overly decorated stuff that's rampant in "adult coloring books").  However, this book is so irresistibly  cute and sweet, I just had to buy.  So irresistibly fun and wholesome that I purchased three copies: one for myself, and two stealth elf attacks.  I put two in gift bags with a set of colored pencils, some herbal tea, and some honey straws, and had them delivered to two ladies, secret Santa style.  There are so many of these "nose gnomes" books now, it'd be easy to think Goodridge's spin on them would get lost in the shuffle.  They're so adorable, they  inspired a pathetic, middle-aged, spinster Ms. Grinch was to do something good.  My elf conspirator reported that both young-at-heart, beautiful souls were delighted with their wholesome holiday sneak attack gifts.  Curse you, Goodridge, curse you!  ;-)Awesome work, Teresa.  Keep the gnomes coming.  All joking aside, you're a talented artist, putting some magic back in the every day world with these books.
